paragraphs.text: Formula verification skill and SymPy CLI for DeepSeek Harness
# dsh-formula-verify
A DeepSeek Harness skill for **verifying paper formulas with executable checks** instead of trusting
arness skill for **verifying paper formulas with executable checks** instead of trusting chat prose.
It turns a formula into:

- a SymPy symbolic check (`simplify(lhs - rhs) == 0`),
- numeric samples at deterministic points,
-
a reusable formula card plus a `pytest` file.
The skill is model-invocable and user-invocable. It ships a self-bootstrapping Python CLI; the first
run creates a private SymPy environment under `$DSH_HOME/formula-verify/venv`.

## Use
Ask the agent to verify a formula, or run the CLI directly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Commands:
| Command | Use |

| `check --lhs ... --rhs ...` | identity / equivalence |
| `check --expr ...` | check that an expres

sion is zero |
| `diff --expr ... --var x` | derivative |
| `integrate --expr ... --var x [--lower a

--upper b]` | indefinite/definite integral |
| `eval --expr ... --values 'x=2' --digits 30` | high-

precision evaluation |
| `simplify --expr ...` | canonical simplification |
| `latex --expr ...` | r

ender to LaTeX |
| `test --path formulas/` | run formula-card pytest in the private environment |
|
`setup` | prewarm the private SymPy environment |
`check` returns:

- `verdict: "symbolic"` — SymPy proved the difference is zero;
- `verdict: "numeric"` — samples agre

ed, but this is **not a proof**;
- `verdict: "failed"` — at least one check disagreed (exit code 1).

## Formula Lab panel
The bundle also ships a **Formula Lab** panel in the right Sidebar:
- Install the bundle from the **Plugins** page with `git+https://github.com/lizyoko9/dsh-formula-ver

ify`, then reload DSH.
- Open the right Sidebar `+` and choose **Formula Lab**.
- Pick a `.tex`, `.p
df`, `.md`, `.mmd` or `.markdown` file from the workspace, set the output directory, and press **Con

vert & extract**.
- For a PDF, choose Mathpix (host env `MATHPIX_APP_ID` / `MATHPIX_APP_KEY`) or an

external command such as MinerU; direct PDF extraction is the lossy fallback.
- The panel shows the
section-grouped report; click a card, `report.md` or `index.md` to open it in the document preview.
The panel stays mounted across tab switches; a preview opens as a normal tab in the same pane, never
mounted across tab switches; a preview opens as a normal tab in the same pane, never as a new split.
The panel calls a local host route protected by a per-process token injected into the DSH index; the
Python CLI is never exposed to other pages. If you already installed the plain filesystem skill, re
move `~/.dsh/skills/formula-verify` before installing the bundle so the same skill is not registered
/.dsh/skills/formula-verify` before installing the bundle so the same skill is not registered twice.
## From a paper (TeX or PDF)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- TeX is the reliable source: `equation`, `align`, `gather`, `multline`, `eqnarray`, `$$...$$` and `

\[...\]` are extracted with section, source line, label and context.
- PDF is a fallback: candidate

lines are extracted with pypdf and marked `needs-latex`; convert them to LaTeX before trusting.
- `p

aper extract` also accepts `.md`, `.markdown` and `.mmd` from Mathpix, MinerU or Nougat.
- To conver

also accepts `.md`, `.markdown` and `.mmd` from Mathpix, MinerU or Nougat.
- To convert a PDF first:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Mathpix uploads the PDF to `api.mathpix.com`; `--backend command` runs a shell command, so only use

converters you trust.
- The extractor writes `eq-*.md` cards (the formula is a display-math block),

`test_eq_*.py` stubs, `index.md`, a section-grouped `report.md` and `report.json`.
- Auto-probe stat
uses: `verified-symbolic`, `numeric-evidence`, `probe-failed`, `definition`, `needs-modeling`, `unpa

rsed`, `needs-latex`.
- Extraction is a draft: review, fill assumptions, replace the skipped pytest
stub with the real model, then run `test`.
## Limits

- SymPy is not a proof assistant. `symbolic` is strong evidence, not a formal proof.
- The LaTeX par
ser handles common paper syntax; unsupported constructs can be passed in SymPy form (`Integral(exp(-

x**2), (x, 0, oo))`).
- Numeric checks use real, mostly positive sample points; domain edges must be

checked explicitly.
- Units/dimensions are not checked by the CLI; add a unit library or a manual c

heck for physical formulas.
- Logic, protocols and algorithms need a truth table, SAT/SMT, TLA+, All
oy or Lean; the skill says when to escalate.
